title: A core's status change writes its own Part History entry
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test, with a Core Charge above $0, so it has a core described Core for followed by part A's description.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the part A row.
  2. Click Inactive under Part Status.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Type Core follows in the Note (Optional) field.
  5. Click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  6. Open the core's own Part History page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens.

Step 2:

  • Inactive is picked.

Step 3:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 4:

  • The note reads Core follows.

Step 5:

  • Part A leaves the Active tab.

Step 6:

  • The page is the core's own: its part details name it Core for followed by part A's description, and its newest entry is "Deactivated | Reason: Core follows".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk), story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part)

  • S10-R19: “A core's status change writes its own Part History entry on the core.”
  • S2-R17: “A part's core becomes inactive together with the part, in the same change.”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
